Low-frequency 2-D DCT pooling

Source: R/hierarchy_poolers.R
dct_pool.Rd

Projects each channel's activation map onto the lowest ny x nx modes of a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (DCT-II). The result summarizes where a channel is active as a mean plus a few smooth spatial contrasts (left versus right, top versus bottom, centre versus edges, and so on).

Usage

dct_pool(ny, nx, order = c("zigzag", "raster"))

Arguments

ny, nx

Number of retained DCT modes along height and width. Neither may exceed the size of the activation map it is applied to.

order

"zigzag" (default) or "raster".

Value

An imfeatures_pooler that yields ny * nx columns per channel.

Details

Mode (v, u) has v half-cycles along height and u half-cycles along width. All ny * nx modes with v < ny and u < nx are kept.

Scale of the coefficients

The mode (0, 0) is rescaled to be the spatial mean, so the first column of each channel equals global_average_pool. All other modes use the orthonormal DCT-II basis. Their coefficients grow with the square root of the number of positions: a unit-amplitude cosine pattern gives a coefficient near 9.9 on a 14 x 14 map and near 158 on a 224 x 224 map. Columns from different modes or different stages are therefore not on a common scale. Standardize the columns before you combine them. block_pca does so by default (feature_scale = "sd").

Column order and names

Columns are ordered by channel, then by mode. order = "zigzag" sorts modes from low to high frequency along anti-diagonals, as in JPEG: (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (2,0), (1,1), (0,2), .... order = "raster" sorts them row by row. Both orders keep the same modes; only the column order differs. Names take the form stage::channel_001::dct_y0_x1, where y and x are the zero-based frequencies v and u.

See also

poolers for the other pooling options, and vgg16_block_end_spec for a ready-made VGG-16 spec that uses DCT pooling.

Examples

# A channel that is active only on the left half of a 6 x 6 map
a <- array(0, dim = c(1, 6, 6, 1))
a[1, , 1:3, 1] <- 1
out <- pool_activations(dct_pool(2, 2), a)
colnames(out) <- pooler_feature_names(dct_pool(2, 2), "b3", 1)
round(out, 3)
#>      b3::channel_001::dct_y0_x0 b3::channel_001::dct_y0_x1
#> [1,]                        0.5                      2.732
#>      b3::channel_001::dct_y1_x0 b3::channel_001::dct_y1_x1
#> [1,]                          0                          0
# dct_y0_x0 is the mean (0.5); dct_y0_x1 carries the left-right contrast.
